why: Fewer, concrete words and a hands-on 'map your bet' action; A is a recited framework with a dated name-drop.
Shorter, keeps the author's own voice and the core point; A's opening adds low-value setup sentences.
The guess prompt comes before the answer, which is the right order; B asks for the guess after the answer is revealed.
Shorter; B's 'shape the rules together' adds a low-value sentence.
B's added sentence is vague and unneeded; A is shorter.
'One session at a time' matches the unit the course uses; 'run' is vague.
The title carries the claim, which saves a closing sentence, and B's 'The generalisation' is an abstract label.
Shorter; B's closer 'flywheel' is a made-up highlight and the M6 aside is hard to picture.
Fewer words; B's added clause is a restatement.

Cut the extra 'This is your side-quest lane' sentence; fewer words.

B adds a low-value closer and an overclaim-ish restatement; shorter wins.
